crg.caveat: `build` + `visualize --format json` produce the artifact; `graph.db` is excluded from the byte comparison because a SQLite page layout is not the tool's output contract. `code-review-graph install` runs only in X2's documented-sync arm and only with HOME, XDG_* and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed inside bench/.competitors/home
crg.syncMechanism: platform hooks plus a watcher. `code-review-graph install` detects the installed AI coding tools, writes their MCP config and installs platform-native hooks/skills where the platform supports them; those hooks and supported commit hooks trigger `update`, which diffs changed files, walks the graph's own import and call edges to find dependents, and re-parses only the files whose SHA-256 changed. For editors without hooks there is `code-review-graph watch` (single repo) and `crg-daemon` (multi-repo background watcher). `code-review-graph update` is the manual incremental path. Freshness is not verified against the tree; the graph is refreshed, never checked.

graphify.caveat: run through `graphify update .` (the documented no-LLM rebuild) rather than the `/graphify .` slash command, which needs a model; graph.html is excluded from the byte comparison because it is a viewer, not the graph. `graphify hook install` is run in X2's documented-sync arm, where the hooks it writes go into the repo copy's own .git/hooks; `graphify install`, which writes a global CLAUDE.md section and a Claude Code PreToolUse hook, is not run
graphify.syncMechanism: git hooks. `graphify hook install` writes post-commit and post-checkout hooks that rebuild the graph in the background (AST only, no API cost) plus a git merge driver that union-merges graph.json. `git pull` / `git merge` are NOT covered: the README tells the user to run `graphify update .` afterwards. Separately, `graphify install` writes a CLAUDE.md section and a Claude Code PreToolUse hook (`graphify hook-guard`) that nudges the assistant to query the graph before grepping; that hook reads the graph, it does not refresh it. There is no mechanical staleness check equivalent to `greplost verify`.

ua.caveat: distributed only as a Claude Code plugin, and `/understand` is a multi-agent LLM pipeline: there is no headless CLI, so the only way to drive it is `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/understand-anything-plugin -p "/understand"` against a clone pinned at v2.9.0, inside the scratch HOME. That spends model tokens on every commit of every metric, so this harness does not run it and never installs the plugin into the machine’s real Claude Code configuration

ua.syncMechanism: git post-commit hook, opt-in. `/understand --auto-update` installs a post-commit hook that incrementally patches the graph so each commit lands with a matching graph. Without it, freshness relies on re-running `/understand`, which is incremental: the skill reads `.ua/meta.json`, takes `gitCommitHash`, runs `git diff <last-hash>..HEAD --name-only` and re-analyzes only the changed files. Re-analysis of a changed file is an LLM pass, so staying fresh costs tokens. There is no verify/staleness gate beyond that commit-hash comparison.

The confidence=high arm (greplost's S3 gate, graphify's and crg's `EXTRACTED` tier) is reported beside it in each cell's detail; scoring greplost at high while scoring a competitor at every confidence would flatter greplost on precision by construction.

X4: every tool is built twice on the same tree, each build in its own process, and the differing bytes of its documented artifact files are counted after trimming the common prefix and suffix (an upper bound on the edit distance, exact for a single contiguous change). greplost is compared over the structure artifacts `listStructurePaths` enumerates; viewer and database files are excluded per competitor, and each cell's `caveat` says which.
